summary: This work demonstrates a $\cos(2\varphi)$ transmon qubit using a KITE (Kinetic Interference co-Tunneling Element) operating in the soft transmon regime with qubit frequency $\omega_q/2\pi = 13.6$ MHz and $\mathcal{E}_{J2}/\mathcal{E}_C = 22$, achieving charge protection via Cooper-pair-parity symmetry. The measured $T_1 = 70$ µs and $T_2^\mathrm{echo} = 2.5$ µs are limited by $1/f$ flux noise ($A_\Phi = 5.6$ µ$\Phi_0$/Hz) rather than dielectric loss, with a 100-fold suppression of the charge matrix element demonstrating protection at a level that places dielectric decay limits above 10 ms.
motivation: Protected qubits with embedded symmetries reduce dominant error channels, and the $\cos(2\varphi)$ qubit leverages charge-parity symmetry to suppress charge noise; however, previous implementations either operated in the light Cooper-pair-box regime (broad 4 GHz charge dispersion) or only demonstrated control between plasmonic transitions away from the symmetry point.
method: A superconducting device consisting of a 0.2 mm$^2$ niobium island shunted through a KITE element composed of two small junctions and superinductive arrays (150 junctions per arm) was fabricated on silicon and measured in a dilution refrigerator with cQED readout at 4.3 GHz. The KITE selectively transmits Cooper-pair doublets, creating a $\cos(2\varphi)$ potential; control and readout exploited residual asymmetry (3% relative mismatch) for coupling to the charge drive line.
result: Single-shot readout achieved 83% fidelity in 5 µs integration (effective temperature 400 µK); coherent Rabi oscillations demonstrated control with $\Omega_\mathrm{Rabi} = 2\pi \times 1$ MHz, Ramsey decay $T_2^\mathrm{Ramsey} = 1.4$ µs; charge protection suppressed the island charge matrix element to $1.3 \times 10^{-2}$ (vs. $2.2$ for unprotected plasmon transition), with theory predictions from Eq. (3) placing dielectric-induced decay limits above 10 ms compared to measured $T_1$ limited by flux noise.
